title: Run i18n:lock only after actually translating; re-stamping untranslated English passes every gate
body: translation.lock.json holds one hash per SPANISH string and nothing for English, on purpose: Spanish is always edited first, so the lock only answers 'did the Spanish this English came from move since?'. Catching silent English-only edits would need a second hash per field and a second check for a mistake the workflow forbids; do not add one. Trap: `pnpm run i18n:lock` stamps whatever is in content.en.json, good, bad or copy-pasted Spanish. i18n.check.ts only catches an EXACT copy over 40 characters, so running the lock without translating declares the work done. Same shape as `format:data` and `og:local`: gates against forgetting, not against lying. Before stamping, confirm every path test:i18n named was really translated; reviewers read the English diff like a number.
not_derivable: Why only Spanish is hashed and that a re-stamp proves nothing are not stated in i18n-lock.ts or i18n.check.ts.

evidence.summary: Hashes every Spanish translatable string; checks nothing.
Missing-translation check: byte-identical and over 40 chars.
